GAME IS PULLING YOUR DESKTOP AUDIO!

I was playing with a random player and he asked why my mic was so quiet. I didn't even have a mic Plugged in. My mic is detachable and during the early hours of the morning, I keep it unplugged since in my current living space, people are asleep in the same room my computer is in.

So I go and check: Open mic is off, and it's still pulling my DESKTOP AUDIO and streaming it through to him! Very quietly, but still. He could overhear me listening to a youtube video.

Then, very quietly, I could hear his keyboard clicking. So I told him that I could hear him typing. He checked his settings and found that his mic was set to off as well!

That is VERY sketch, and the only way to really turn voice chat off is to turn your input to 0. But that makes me wonder what they're doing pulling Desktop audio at all?

So, I almost never leave a review on a game let alone post.  And while the game play itself is fun and engaging especially with friends. Just something mindless to get into and the rogue like elements work... I have to post a negative review due to the terrible experience for ultrawide monitor support.

There is no excuse in this day and age to have 0 support for ultrawide. 
Playing Full screen results in weird ghosting and offset UI elements.
On some maps the ghosting is so bad that it's unplayable.
No resolution at full screen fixes this issue.

Now, if I play in some form of windowed mode, it does fix the issue, but I run into a different issue. Given the nature of the game and constant mouse movements, inevitably, my cursor will be outside of the game window and when firing I will click the desktop or some other app. This causes me to lose focus on the game which results in my character standing there and taking damage.

I have not yet found a way to lock the cursor to the game window. No, I will not use a 3rd party app to achieve this, I shouldn't have to.

So until this issue is fixed for ultrawide monitor users, I can't recommend this game.

That will make the game more accessible because the time limits to finish levels is limited. There are upsides. The game animations, how the game flows and feels, almost seems godly and scary. It's like how Arcade machines used to be. Smooth and looking very spiffy.  This game matches the arcade style.

Honestly, this game has a lot of promise but matchmaking being "broken" is what is keeping me from playing.

The gist is this.
The game has various maps and modes. Each of these maps has a range or tiers of difficulty that you can choose. The difficulty not only effects what you might encounter, but also enemy AI and move sets. 

The problem is that matchmaking is limited to only the tier of difficulty you have selected. So if you dont have friends with which to play, or are not at the highest tiers, you are likely to never be matched because there is no cross-tier compatibility

I think the biggest issue the game has for me personally is how overly weighted towards co-op it is. I play a lot of games with co-op in them, I generally prefer them, but I don't always co-op in them either. Another game to look at from recent memory for this is Elden Ring Nightreign. That game launched in a state that pretty much said "either get two of your friends to play with you, or you better hope matchmaking is kind to you for once." 

Almost immediately a lot of people had a problem with this, either because they only had one friend they really wanted to or could play it with and the game just really didn't have any intention to balance for duos at the time, or because the intended single player balancing still needed a lot of work. Since then, they have worked on both of those things and I've heard good things about it, but admittedly can't really speak from experience on solo or duo myself.

This game is very similar in that regard. You'll either want a dedicated group to play in so you all advance through the content's difficulty gating at the same time as each other, or you'll need to group up with randoms who are working on the same thing as you. You can solo, but it's just going to make it more apparent how much the game is balanced around a full group whether you succeed or not. Things will just start taking longer because two major sources of damage aren't there with you.

TL;DR: Include and incentivize co-op? Yes. Kind of sort of include but pretty heavily disincentivize solo play? No, thank you, not for me.

The game’s controls are excellent—smooth, responsive, and snappy. Unfortunately, that’s about the only real praise I can give it. Performance was mostly fine for me aside from occasional stuttering, but the bigger problem is how much the game wastes your time with mobile-style “claim this reward” pop-ups and a crappy battle pass. You constantly have to click through meaningless rewards, which would be easier to forgive if the core game were better. 

Most of your power comes from permanent progression rather than the roguelite upgrades you choose during a run. Whether you’re stacking burn on enemies, freezing them, or triggering large music pulses, these upgrades barely affect your playstyle. The enemies are so easy that there’s no challenge to begin with—I even completed a run without picking up any upgrades and didn’t notice any drop in efficiency.

The bosses are a pretty good, but they’re nothing you haven’t seen in other games. Worse, they’re frequently recycled, and there aren’t enough unique ones to keep things fresh, so the experience goes stale quickly. Normal enemies are even worse: they’re weak, require no strategy or skill, and feel like they exist only to waste your time. If the builds were interesting, this wouldn’t matter as much because I could at least have fun experimenting—but as it stands, they’re just as underwhelming.

EDIT: I have dyslexia so I wrote a review and slapped it into chatgpt for proofreading. It's still an accurate review. I'd rather have unnecessary hyphens all over the place than have it not be readable.

I just want to clear up some misinformation in these reviews on the subject of ransomware (spoiler, this game is NOT RANSOMWARE)

To the people saying ransomware... You need to learn what the words you say mean before you throw them around. This is annoying. I'll go ahead and explain what ransomware is an isn't. Ransomware is a type of malware (virus) that disrupts your PC's functionality unless you pay. It will show a pop-up with some kind of demand, AKA, a ransom note. Which is where the name comes from. What it (ransomware) isn't... is literally anything else.

The reason people are making this claim is that there's a pop-up asking to make changes to your drive when you install the game. Which... is actually perfectly normal. Lots of games do this. The reason we're seeing a lot of this in THESE reviews is probably because of bad timing with some phrase a bunch of misinformed people are seeing on the internet, and because the game is free, which attracts younger users, who are more likely to be misinformed.

In other words, the people claiming this is ransomware are just trying to sound smart by using a word they don't understand to explain something that scares them because they don't understand it, and don't understand that it's perfectly normal.
